title: Bitcoin ETFs approach $1B in 7-session inflow run
summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $69 million in inflows on Wednesday, extending their inflow streak to seven sessions and bringing total inflows during the period to nearly $1 billion

title: Kakao taps Circle to explore won stablecoin payment infrastructure
summary: Kakao Group and Circle signed an MOU to explore won stablecoin payments, remittances, merchant settlement and tokenized financial services.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.

title: Swiss bank BancaStato launches regulated crypto trading with Sygnum
summary: Swiss cantonal bank BancaStato integrated Sygnum’s crypto trading and custody services into its Avaloq-powered digital banking apps for Bitcoin and other assets.

title: White House accuses Moonshot AI of distilling Anthropic tech for K3
summary: US officials warn that Chinese firms conducting covert, industrial-scale AI distillation could face sanctions and export restrictions.

title: SEC settles Coinbase suit over ‘text messages that disappeared’
summary: The settlement follows a watchdog report last year that blamed “avoidable errors” for the loss of nearly a year’s worth of Gary Gensler’s text messages.

title: Hackers steal $31.6M in 2 crypto bridge attacks within 7 hours
summary: AFX, a decentralized perpetual exchange operating on Arbitrum, reportedly lost $24.15 million on Wednesday, while the Verus Ethereum bridge was attacked hours later.

title: S&P launches blockchain fundamentals index for digital assets
summary: The benchmark tracks blockchain networks using protocol revenue, offering an alternative to traditional market capitalization-weighted crypto indexes.

title: Crypto PAC pours $1M into Michigan Democratic primary race
summary: Donavan McKinney, running against Michigan incumbent Shri Thanedar, said that “the crypto lobby is paying my opponent back for helping Trump“ with the PAC-funded ads.

title: US officials barred until 2029 from issuing or sponsoring tokens under CLARITY’s proposed ethics rules
summary: According to Senator Cynthia Lummis, one of the bill’s advocates, the ethics language would apply to US presidents’ crypto ventures, including Donald Trump’s.
